title: Architecture onramp / Redwood eval - Nova Ventures
summary: Intro discovery focusing on how Nova Ventures would integrate Redwood across their platform. Customer is exploring hosted for fast testing, dedicated for predictable throughput, and private for data residency. Key constraints: latency SLOs for chat assistant (sub-200ms token), quota enforcement per-tenant, and deep observability hooks into tracing and token-level cost. SE demo plans and a benchmarking pilot were agreed as next steps.
next_steps: Redwood to send hosted + dedicated pricing sheet and a rough sizing estimate (Maya)
SE to run a baseline perf test using Nova sample prompts and return results (Jonas)
Nova to provide sample prompt set, traffic profile, and example LangChain flows (Priya)
Schedule technical deep dive to look at VPC/private deployment options and SSO/KMS (week of 2026-04-20)
action_items: Maya Chen: Share pricing + quick wins doc and link to hosted trial console (due: 2026-04-15)
Jonas Patel: Run perf baseline (quantized and non-quant) against their prompts, include p95 latency and token cost (due: 2026-04-20)
Priya Nair: Upload sample prompt set, LangChain recipes, and traffic histogram to shared drive (due: 2026-04-13)
Eli Martinez: Confirm security reviewer contact for SOC 2 / ISO artifacts (due: 2026-04-14)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-11
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonas Patel (Redwood SE), Eli Martinez (CTO, Nova), Priya Nair (Platform Eng), Samir Gupta (ML Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Customer evaluating Redwood for multi-mode deployment. Primary focus on integration surface area: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy patterns, per-tenant quotas, and observability hooks.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, really appreciate you making time today, um this is just an architecture onramp to understand how Nova would integrate Redwood. quick intros?
[00:12] Eli Martinez: sure, eli here, cto at nova, we run a data platform that supports a bunch of internal apps, looking to add a conversational assistant and some embeddings search, timelines tight, quarterish.
[00:22] Priya Nair: priya, platform eng, i'll be owning the integration with our api gateway and service mesh.
[00:28] Samir Gupta: samir, ml eng, i'll own the prompt sets and reuse with langchain.
[00:34] Jonas Patel: jonas from redwood, i focus on infra and integration patterns, happy to dig into SDKs, langchain connectors, and perf.

[02:05] Maya Chen: big picture — are you leaning hosted first or do you have procurement constraints pushing you toward dedicated/private?
[02:18] Eli Martinez: we'd like a quick PoC on hosted for speed but if the numbers look good we'd move to dedicated; private might be needed for certain regulated customers. security and audit logs are huge.
[02:30] Priya Nair: also we have an internal quota model — we need per-tenant token quotas and hard rate limits at the gateway, so we need to know how Redwood enforces quotas or if we should do that in our proxy.

[03:12] Jonas Patel: sounds good. on quotas we support both client-side and server-side enforcement. for hosted we have token-level usage and per-api-key quotas you can map to tenants; you can also run a proxy layer that does pre-checks. for dedicated/private you can push enforcement into the edge router with our SDK hooks.
[03:40] Samir Gupta: when you say sdk hooks what are you thinking, like a middleware that intercepts requests?
[03:46] Jonas Patel: yeah middleware or sidecar. our node/python sdk exposes a request hook and a pre-send callback so you can attach tenant-id, trace id, cost center etc. langchain connectors we provide are thin wrappers — they pass through metadata so telemetry stays intact.

[05:22] Priya Nair: can you integrate with our existing api gateway? we run envoy + istio service mesh, and we'd like a gateway pattern so calls from our apps go through our proxy then to redwood, not direct from client browsers.
[05:38] Jonas Patel: that's a common pattern. we often recommend a proxy because it gives you control over authentication, tenant mapping, and throttling. we have examples for envoy filters and a sample sidecar that handles token caching and batching.
[06:03] Maya Chen: note: i will share the envoy example repo after the call.

[06:30] Eli Martinez: latency — our chat assistant needs sub-200ms token latency for the fast paths, p95 ideally. how realistic is that on hosted vs dedicated?
[06:44] Jonas Patel: short answer: dedicated with reserved GPUs and tuned batching gets you consistent p95s that are much lower. hosted can get there for smaller seq lengths but variability is higher due to multi-tenant scheduling. and kv cache/prefix caching matters: if you're serving repeated contexts caching will shave tokens off.
[07:12] Samir Gupta: "kv cache" = key value cache for attention past?
[07:16] Jonas Patel: yeah sometimes transcribed as k v cache in our docs, but yes the attention cache. we also offer prefix caching where common prompts are memoized.

[08:05] Priya Nair: observability is critical. we need traces that correlate user requests through our gateway to redwood tokens and cost. do you expose open telemetry spans and token-level cost breakdowns?
[08:20] Jonas Patel: yes — we can emit OTLP spans and also export token-level metrics to prometheus. console shows token breakdown by prompt/response. you can also ingest traces into your datadog/tempo. sometimes names in spans get mangled by exporters — little gotchas there.

[09:10] Eli Martinez: what about langchain and llamindex integrations — we use langchain heavy in our orchestration layer and LlamaIndex for doc retrieval. do you have adapters? any pitfalls?
[09:25] Jonas Patel: we maintain official langchain wrappers and a community llamaindex connector. the wrappers preserve streaming and function calling semantics. pitfalls: be careful with automatic retry logic in langchain chains — it can double count tokens if retries happen at the SDK layer. we recommend disabling chain-level retries and letting the SDK handle idempotency.

[11:00] Maya Chen: question on security/compliance — you'll want SOC 2 and also KMS/HSM integrations for private. do you have an on-prem package?
[11:12] Jonas Patel: yes, private deployment supports customer-managed KMS, HSM integration, and an air-gapped installer. audit logs are turned on by default in private. hosted customers get audit logs exported to S3 or their SIEM.
[11:36] Priya Nair: must confirm data residency — can you restrict model hosting to eu-west-1 for EU customers?
[11:43] Jonas Patel: yes region pinning is supported for dedicated/private; for hosted we have region controls but cross-region fallback exists for capacity. we'll capture requirements in the next step.

[14:15] Eli Martinez: curious about token cost. we have an embeddings-heavy search product and cost-per-embedding matters; do you offer batching/caching recommendations?
[14:28] Jonas Patel: Redwood Optimize will profile workloads and recommend batching and quantization configs. for embeddings we recommend bulk batch inferencing and caching top-k vectors in our recommended pipeline; we can also run a recompute job to re-embed with quantized models for cost reduction.

[15:10] Samir Gupta: for the PoC we'd want to try two paths: 1) quick hosted prototype plugged into our langchain flows, 2) a dedicated perf baseline with a representative load. is that feasible?
[15:22] Maya Chen: yes that's exactly the flow we recommend. small hosted pilot for feature validation, then dedicated sizing + perf run if results look good.

[16:05] Priya Nair: about quotas again — if we put quotas in the proxy, how do we reconcile billing with Redwoods per-token metering? we need to avoid double accounting.
[16:20] Jonas Patel: good question. we surface per-api-key metering and you can map those api-keys to tenant ids. many customers do throttling in their proxy but reconcile billing by having the proxy attach the tokenized usage header and we export per-tenant usage reports for reconciliation. sometimes small discrepancies occur due to streaming commits.

[18:00] Eli Martinez: what's the SDK footprint? we run node services and go microservices; do you have a go sdk?
[18:12] Jonas Patel: official sdks: python, node; community-supported go and java clients. the go client includes the same hooks but sometimes community clients lag behind with streaming. we'd be happy to share an api surface doc.

[19:30] Samir Gupta: function calling and structured outputs — we rely on function outputs to call our internal services. does Redwood support schema enforcement and strict typing?
[19:45] Jonas Patel: yes function calling is supported and we also have schema validators at the SDK level. edge cases: nested json can sometimes be garbled by transcription or streaming chunk boundaries; the SDK has helpers to reassemble.

[21:05] Maya Chen: a few gotchas we've seen: 1) if you run LlamaIndex + LangChain, watch for 2x token usage when you materialize intermediate representations; 2) retries in upper layers; 3) using the wrong model size for inference. we'll share a checklist.

[22:40] Priya Nair: cc: on observability — can we get log links that include request ids so our SREs can pivot from our trace to your logs?
[22:52] Jonas Patel: yes request-id passthrough is supported, and the console supports deep links back to the raw request logs. for private we can ship logs to your splunk/elastic cluster.

[24:10] Eli Martinez: cost controls — can we set hard spend ceilings per-team?
[24:22] Jonas Patel: yes we have quotas and spend alerts at the api-key level and you can set hard caps that will reject requests when exceeded (soft vs hard). hosted caps are immediate; with dedicated there's also commit-level accounting.

[26:00] Samir Gupta: can we experiment with quantized model variants for the dedicated run? eager to see delta between int8 vs fp16 on quality.
[26:12] Jonas Patel: absolutely. we can provision quantized variants and run side-by-side evals. our Optimize tooling will suggest quantization and batching settings by workload.

[28:30] Maya Chen: timeline? Eli mentioned end of quarter. what's a realistic ramp?
[28:40] Eli Martinez: if hosted PoC goes well we want to be ready to ship internal beta in 6 weeks, public facing in 3 months, but that depends on perf/privacy sign off.
[29:00] Maya Chen: sounds tight but feasible. we should aim to run the perf baseline next week or two, then a technical deep dive for private deployment.

[31:15] Priya Nair: procurement questions — what contract terms exist for dedicated capacity, is there a minimum commit?
[31:28] Maya Chen: typical dedicated commitments start at $X/month (Maya will follow up with specifics) and we have monthly and annual options; pricing depends on GPU class and runway.

[33:00] Eli Martinez: any red flags from infra side we should know?
[33:08] Jonas Patel: sometimes folks underestimate data egress for embeddings pipelines. also watch out for KV cache sizing if you keep large contexts in memory, that affects GPU memory planning.

[35:40] Samir Gupta: for our langchain flow, how do you handle streaming back to client UIs? we want real-time partial tokens.
[35:50] Jonas Patel: streaming is supported end-to-end. our SDK provides event streams and chunked responses; when you run through a proxy you need to ensure it forwards chunked transfer-encoding rather than buffering. we have nginx/envoy configs for that.

[37:00] Priya Nair: ok on SSO — we'd like SAML/SCIM for user provisioning for the console and RBAC.
[37:10] Maya Chen: yes SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning supported, plus role-based access controls on per-route/model.

[38:50] Eli Martinez: fine — let's recap next steps and owners.
[39:00] Maya Chen: recap: magna list: send pricing and envoy example (maya), run perf baseline (jonas), customer to upload prompts and traffic (priya), schedule deep dive (maya/jonas + priya/eli). any other?
[39:20] Priya Nair: i'll also invite our security reviewer to the deep dive.

[41:00] Jonas Patel: one more note: when you run the perf baseline please include p50/p95/p99 and a mix of short and long seq lengths; streaming latencies look different than batch latencies.

[42:30] Eli Martinez: got it. thanks all. quick question from my side — do you have a checklist for moving from hosted to dedicated?
[42:45] Maya Chen: yes we'll share the migration playbook with steps, config flags, and validation tests.

[44:20] Priya Nair: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[44:25] Samir Gupta: thanks, we'll try to get the prompts uploaded tomorrow.
[44:32] Maya Chen: perfect, we'll follow up with links and the pricing doc.
[44:40] Eli Martinez: thanks, bye.
[44:45] Meeting ends.
